newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Steady ahead of key data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Steady ahead of key data.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were steady to slightly higher late Monday, as short-covering helped boost debt futures ahead of the first of two key employment reports due this week.
"The overall market was unchanged to up one-eighth. Your high-grades were unchanged to slightly better, and your dollar bonds closed quoted up one-eighth," said a municipal bond analyst.

The first-quarter U.S. Employment Cost Index, a yardstick of how much it costs employers to pay their workers and provide them with benefits, was scheduled for release at 0830 EDT (1230 GMT) on Tuesday.

The data, along with the April payrolls report due Friday, were expected to be give traders a clearer sign of whether the Federal Reserve might leave interest rates unchanged or raise them again when its policy-making arm meets on May 20.
Further, the National Association of Purchasing Management will release its April report on Thursday at 1000 EDT (1400 GMT), giving the market a fresh look at how the manufacturing sector is faring.
"I still think people are going to go in short, but a lot of people are putting on positions," a trader said.
"Weaker shorts are just getting out of the market," he added, referring to the late-day gains posted by U.S. Treasury bond and municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade.
The employment cost index was forecast to show a 0.9 percent rise, according to a survey of economists by Reuters.
And the April payrolls were estimated to rise 211,000, up from February's gain of 175,000 jobs, while the unemployment rate was seen as flat at 5.2 percent.

While the market was wary that the reports would show unexpected strength, that was not the only concern. Traders said the market might be left rudderless if the data failed to present a convincing picture of either an accelerating or slowing economy.
The recent rise in yields already appears to have made it unprofitable for at least some municipal issuers to refund outstanding bonds.
"I think you're already looking at a lighter refunding calendar than we had," a trader said. "Unless you get a substantial rally in here, we're probably going to be a lower level of issuance."
Municipal bond sales for Tuesday, April 29, were expected to total $1.6 billion in 30 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Negotiated offerings added up to $1.3 billion in 14 sales, with a $640 million New York City Municipal Water Agency deal through J.P. Morgan Securities Inc topping the list. The deal was being watched keenly to see if it would draw as much demand as Friday's $932 million sale by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, which drew strong demand despite various delays in bringing the deal to the market.

While that sale benefited from a scarcity of New Jersey paper, traders said the water bond sale should help show if demand for New York's debt has abated. The New York State Thruway next week plans to sell around $350 million of revenue bonds.
In debt futures, the June Municipal contracts gained 11 ticks to 112-18/32, while the June T-bond contracts rose nine ticks to 107-13/32. The MOB spread was at plus 165 ticks.
In the secondary market, Chicago, Illinois, Board of Education Chicago School Reform of December 2020, which pay a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 6.04 percent, NET, down one basis point.
And Siekeston, Missouri, Electricity Revenue Refundings of June 2022, which pay a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.89 percent, NET, up one basis point.
